\subsection{FPR-recalibration recipes}
\label{app:fpr-recipes}

\begin{table}[h]
  \centering
  \caption{\textbf{FPR-recalibration recipes evaluated on $n{=}3000$
    non-watermarked samples (1000 per model, 60/40 calibration/test
    split).} Goal: empirical FPR $\le$ 1\% with TPR = 100\%.
    \textbf{Fix~1} (recompute the threshold from the empirical SD of
    $z$ on a non-watermarked corpus) and \textbf{Fix~5} (HDD-lite,
    inverse-frequency-weighted statistic) both hit the target while
    preserving 100\% TPR. Fix~3 ($k$-skip) collapses TPR because the
    watermark only constrains adjacent transitions.}
  \label{tab:fpr-recipes}
  \small
  \setlength{\tabcolsep}{4pt}
  \begin{tabular}{lll}
    \toprule
    Method & avg FPR & avg TPR \\
    \midrule
    iid baseline (no fix)               & 4.23\% & 100.0\% \\
    \textbf{Fix~1: empirical SD recal.} & \textbf{1.34\%} & \textbf{100.0\%} \\
    Fix~2: Newey--West HAC               & 3.45\% & 100.0\% \\
    Fix~3: $k$-skip ($k{=}3$)           & 2.46\% & 2.2\% (TPR collapse) \\
    Fix~4: stopword filter (top-200)    & 5.18\% & 99.0\% \\
    \textbf{Fix~5: HDD-lite (model-free)} & \textbf{2.35\%} & \textbf{100.0\%} \\
    \bottomrule
  \end{tabular}
\end{table}

\subsection{Empirical FPR=0\% achievability}
\label{app:fpr-zero}

\begin{table}[h]
  \centering
  \caption{\textbf{FPR=0\% by lifting the threshold to
    $z^* = \max_i z_{\mathrm{nwm},i} + 0.5$.} Computed on the

    text retains TPR=100\% because clean MCL $z$ ($\approx$25--40)

\paragraph{Open data and deferred extensions.}
The following experiments are deferred to the extended version of
this paper:
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{DIPPER paraphrase attack.} Grammar-preserving
    paraphrase via DIPPER~\citep{krishna2023paraphrasing} on at least
    one (model, domain) cell.
  \item \textbf{$k$-regular validation at $k\geq 3$.}
    \autoref{thm:k-regular} predicts $p_0 = k/S$ for any
    $k$-regular topology; we validate $k\in\{1,2\}$ only.
  \item \textbf{External-LM PPL or MAUVE quality metric.}
    Self-PPL is conservative but circular; an external judge LM or
    MAUVE would give a model-independent quality reading.
  \item \textbf{Base (non-instruction-tuned) and $\geq 10$B
    LLMs.} Our fleet covers only instruction-tuned 7--8B models.
  \item \textbf{$\rho$-sweep on the new fleet.} The current
    headline runs use $\rho=0.5$ only; the previous gate-invariance
    ablation was on a smaller setup.
  \item \textbf{Adversary with detector-oracle access.}
    \autoref{thm:security} excludes adversaries who can query the
    detector; characterising query complexity is open.
\end{itemize}
